handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 66 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all source verses and every evidence note; see revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 66 verses and every editorial note. The independent reader inspected all 66 source positions and all 33 author notes. Tenerum at line 2 is now clear; the tentative absque at 39 is corrected to arua sine. Additional tentative ending words are recovered at 60 (esse sinant) and 62 (potest). Other faint words, the incomplete marginal title, and the severely faded lower-right gaps remain documented source uncertainty; no expected verse is supplied from another witness. No human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: The large E and three short marginal lines were inspected in the page and enlarged heading. AD is distinguishable; EAM and IS EST remain tentative. The remaining capitals cannot safely supply a complete title, and their gaps remain.
The individual enlargement supports tenerum with distinguishable letters. Its unclear element is removed and the note is now an observation.
The image supports pulchre domine. The source spelling is retained without regularizing the two endings.
Turpiter is compatible with the faint opening. The other words are clearer, and the local qualification remains appropriate.
Image 93 left begins this verse. Ecce recens is pale but compatible with the source; the local uncertainty is retained.
Qua periit aliquis remains compatible with the visible sequence. No expected variant is substituted.
The final pugne is visibly written with e. Its source spelling is retained.
The men of carmen is conspicuously darker and the terminal point is visible. Neither the shade nor the thickened strokes proves an erased prior state or a historical hand.
The terminal pilum is faint but remains compatible with the enlarged traces. Its unclear element is retained.
The initial double-m sequence of ammonitus is visible. The source form is retained.
The pale opening remains compatible with Erati postes. No unattested initial vowel or grammatical correction is inserted.
The central sapiens in munere remains plausible but markedly faded. Its local uncertainty remains; the line is not reconstructed from an expected reading.
The image supports celi saturnus in that order. The manuscript spelling is retained.
The entire bottom-left verse was inspected. It remains compatible with Omne lucrum tenebris alta premebat humus, but its low contrast warrants retaining the complete-line unclear element.
The final word on the upper-right verse has only pale and disturbed traces. A complete word cannot be independently established, so its gap remains.
The visible sequence nulla que is retained with editorial spacing. No reconstruction of a different inflection is imposed.

The enlargement shows a longer sequence with sine distinctly present before uomere; absque does not fit those letters. It is corrected to tentative arua sine, preserving local uncertainty in the crowded first word.
The short word before remo remains ambiguous at low contrast. The tentative eruta is retained without replacing it with a familiar reading.
The dark patch reaches the ending, but fuisses remains readable. The patch does not justify an inferred cancellation.
The final name is crossed by a disturbed dark area. Quirinus remains a tentative decipherment, with no assertion about earlier letters, deletion, or hand.
The opening Liber et alcides remains pale but compatible with the transcription. The subsequent separate et ligature is visible and its declared expansion is retained.
Curia pauperibus remains faint; the later clausa est dat census honores is clearer. Existing local uncertainty is retained.
The full verse was independently inspected. The pale Inde grauis iudex inde seuerus eques remains compatible with the source and stays qualified.
A dark patch crosses the latter portion of forumque. The tentative word is retained under unclear without reconstructing a prior state.
Seruiat hi pacem is compatible with the pale opening. Crudaque bella gerent remains clearer. No normalization is made.
The lower-right area is heavily faded and locally stained. Auidi and amoris remain the defensible tentative fragments; the incomplete ending and other spans remain gaps.
The enlarged ending supports tentative esse sinant after pauperis. These two words are recovered under unclear; the faded opening remains a gap.
The full physical line was enlarged. Ille remains a defensible tentative fragment, but the adjoining pale groups cannot safely establish additional complete words.
After multa, the final letters support tentative potest, now retained in place of the final gap. The preceding faded region remains unreadable.
Custos and maritum remain tentative with clearer illa between them. The intervening traces do not securely distinguish a full word, and its gap remains.
Cede and final domo remain compatible with the image. Other surviving strokes are not completed into a phrase; the gaps remain photographic illegibility, not source omission.
The final couplet begins image 94 left and is followed by the next large initial. Si modo quisquam and amantes remain tentative; the source does not justify an unqualified complete reading.
The enlarged middle remains compatible with the tentative segmentation puluere mutet. No preposition or further ending is imported from another text; the uncertainty is retained.
